Chapter 9: Dealing with Competition—Ignore the Noise and Focus on Your Path
You know, competition is usually painted as this fierce, winner-takes-all battle—like if one business wins, another has to lose. But honestly, that way of thinking just fills you with anxiety and distracts you from what really matters. What if, instead, you put all that energy into your own work—and let everyone else do the same?
Picture two gardeners, each with their own plot. One keeps glancing over the fence, always worried about what the neighbor’s planting. The other? They’re busy nurturing their own soil, watering their plants, and enjoying the process. Who do you think ends up with the healthier, more vibrant garden? It’s almost always the one who stays focused on their own patch.
When you’re glued to what your competitors are doing, it’s easy to slip into imitation mode—copying features, adjusting prices, or latching onto every new trend. But chasing someone else’s moves rarely leads to real, lasting success. Instead, it’s much more powerful to double down on what makes your business unique and valuable.
So, how do you handle competition without getting sidetracked? Here are a few strategies to keep in mind:
First, stay focused on your mission. Let your own values and goals drive every decision, not just whatever your competitors are up to.
Second, make sure you stand out. Highlight what sets you apart, instead of getting caught up in matching everyone else.
Third, avoid those knee-jerk reactions. Don’t change your course just because someone else makes a move.
And finally, celebrate your strengths. Lean into what you do best and let that shine through in everything you offer.
Think about a boutique clothing store. While big chains might race to the bottom with endless discounts, that little shop focuses on offering unique designs and truly personal service. By sticking to its identity, the boutique attracts loyal customers who love what makes it different.
So, here’s the key takeaway: tune out all that background noise. When you focus on your own path, you build resilience, spark innovation, and create value that lasts.
